description: The headless build contract (Features WV3, P10.core; CROSS-ENGINE-FEATURES point 12, "a headless plugin build replaces each engine's template export"; the UI Gauntlet's E6 Build rows, UX-SPEC §7.10, GAP-TOOL7). A build request (world, recipe, packs and lockfile, target, host) is planned or refused with core's codes; a build result (status, artefacts with one primary, logs, refusals or a failure, the inputs echoed) is checked against its request. Engine runners answer plan from their headless build entry in validate-only mode; no engine build code is in core.
sources: core src/build/headless-build.ts (planBuild, checkBuildResult, formatBuildSize; buildRequestSchema, buildResultSchema)
core src/game-genres/recipes.ts (RECIPE_IDS: the recipes core binds)

the Features Gauntlet's CROSS-ENGINE-FEATURES point 12 (each engine's headless route: Godot --headless, Unity -batchmode -nographics -executeMethod, Unreal UnrealEditor-Cmd commandlets, Babylon's headless host)

the UI Gauntlet's UX-SPEC §7.10 Play & ship (Build rows per engine, "Unreal can't build for the web.", "Web build ready · 18 MB · 2 min ago", "The web build failed: {first error}") and GAP-TOOL7 insimul_export_game ({target} → artefact path, size, how to open)
pipelines pipelines/game-export/ (the template export this replaces)

contract.hiddenDetail: the engine's message held a password or token, so it is not shown.

rules.order: credentials first, in the raw request; then the shape (one invalid-request per distinct field the schema rejects, however many of its rules that field breaks; field null for the request as a whole; a request with a wrong shape gets no further check); then paths, target, recipe, packs; then what the context verifies (lockfile, input files, predicate-schema hash). Refusals are listed in refusalCodes order, then by field; notes in noteCodes order, then by field; result and progress issues in issueCodes and progressIssueCodes order, then by field. "By field" is code-unit (ordinal) order of the field strings, a null field as the empty string: UTF-16 code units compared one by one, a prefix first, no locale and no case folding (C# string.CompareOrdinal, Java compareTo; never a locale-aware or case-insensitive compare). A language whose strings are UTF-32 (GDScript, FString on macOS and Linux) compares by code point, which differs only between a supplementary character and one in U+E000-U+FFFF: it compares the UTF-16 encodings. So Token sorts before apiKey, clientSecret before client_secret, U+1F600 before U+FF5A, and packs.enabled.10 before packs.enabled.2. The recipe's file-and-hash pair is checked on the raw request whenever the recipe is an object, so a recipe with a file and no sha256 is invalid-request at recipe.sha256 whatever else is wrong with it (a validator that stops at a type error must still report it)
rules.platform: host resolves to host.os; a plan and a result always name the resolved platform
rules.target: a platform outside enginePlatforms[engine] is target-unsupported; a desktop platform other than host.os is target-not-on-host unless the engine is in crossDesktopEngines
rules.paths: every path is project-relative with / separators: no leading / or ~, no drive letter, no backslash, no empty, . or .. segment (path-outside-project). Only when every path is inside the project: an input path equal to or inside target.outDir is out-dir-holds-inputs, and a target.outDir equal to or inside one of engineReservedDirs[engine] is out-dir-reserved (the engine keeps its project there; a clean build would empty it). Both compare case-folded, inside under either of two folds, because macOS and Windows file systems fold case: each code point on its own (no context, no locale) mapped to its full lower case, that to its full upper case, and that to its full lower case (UnicodeData.txt plus the unconditional mappings of SpecialCasing.txt: ß, ẞ and SS are ss, ﬁ is fi, ŉ is ʼn, İ is i and U+0307, ς σ and Σ are one letter, ı is i). The macOS fold NFD-normalises first and NFC-normalises after (APFS folds with full case folding and ignores normalisation); the Windows fold does not normalise at all (NTFS upper-cases each unit as spelt; normalising first would move U+0345 past other combining marks). A path is inside the folder when it is "equal to or starts with the folder and a /" under the macOS fold OR under the Windows fold. The folds merge at least what APFS and NTFS merge; where they merge more (ı and i on macOS), a build is only refused more often. Never a whole-string lower-casing (it makes a final Σ a ς)
rules.recipe: null is the world's own game; an id alone must be one core binds (unknown-recipe); a file comes with its sha256 and any id; the plan says bound when there is no file
rules.packs: a pack listed twice is duplicate-pack (at its second and every later index); with a lockfile in the context: it must parse as insimul.packs-lock/1 (lock-invalid), be written for the request's engine (lock-engine-mismatch), and install every enabled pack (pack-not-locked, per index). A pending merge proposal or a forked core is a note (lock-pending-merge, core-forked), one per pack, at the pack's first index in packs.enabled
rules.inputs: with files in the context, each input path (world, recipe file, lockfile) must be there (input-missing) with the request's hash (input-changed); without them the plan notes inputs-unverified
rules.predicateSchema: refused only when the world and the context both name a predicate-schema hash and they differ
rules.credentials: a key that is a credential, a non-empty string or a number under a key whose name ends (lower-cased, without _ and -) in token, secret, password, passwd, apikey, accesskey, privatekey, jwt, authorization, cookie, sessionid, databaseurl, dburl, connectionstring or mongouri, or any string holding a JWT, a database URL, a URL with user:password, a Bearer token, or a known model/cloud key shape. Refused in a request (secret-in-request), flagged in a result (secret-in-result); a detail never repeats the value, and a key that is itself a credential is named secretKeyStandIn in the field path
rules.result: the result's requestId, engine, resolved platform, configuration and input hashes equal the request's (checked only when the request parses). refused: core's refusals for the request, same codes and fields in the same order, no error, no artefacts. failed: an error whose code is in failureSteps and whose step is that code's step (any: any step), and an error-level log in that step. succeeded: exactly one primary artefact matching primaryArtefact[platform], no error, no refusals, and a request core plans. A failed or cancelled build that names a primary is status-inconsistent at artefacts.<i>.primary, one per primary; a refused build's artefacts are status-inconsistent once, at artefacts, and a primary among them adds nothing. Every artefact (and logFile) lies strictly inside target.outDir; no path twice (duplicate-artefact at each later index). Result paths compare as spelt, never case-folded: the engine names the files it wrote. Log seq strictly increasing
rules.summary: bytes is every artefact but kind log; open is primaryArtefact[platform].open on success; line: succeeded "<Label> build ready · <size>", failed "The <label> build failed: <error.detail>", refused "The <label> build did not start: <first refusal detail>", cancelled "The <label> build was stopped." (<Label> from platformTitles, <label> from platformLabels). When the result carries a credential in error.detail or any refusal, the engine's words are replaced by hiddenDetail
rules.progress:
a running build writes insimul.build-progress/1 events (requestId, seq, step, fraction 0..1 or null, canStop, elapsedMs, optional message), one JSON object per line on its progress stream, and its result last. The events answer the request (same requestId, checked only when the request parses), seq strictly increases (progress-out-of-order), the step never goes back in steps order, by one step or more (step-went-back; the same step again is fine), a number fraction is never lower than the last number before it, equal allowed, a null between them allowed (fraction-went-back); no credential (secret-in-progress), looked for in whatever was written, a list or not; the shape of the whole list is progress-invalid, one per distinct field. Summary from the last event alone (its own fraction, null included; no earlier fraction is carried forward): step, stepNumber (1-based in steps), steps, fraction, canStop (E6 offers Stop only when true), line "Building…

%" with p = floor(fraction × 100 + 0.5) in IEEE double, else "Building… of "; no event, no summary
rules.size: under 1000: "<n> bytes" ("1 byte"); else kB, MB or GB (decimal), one decimal under 10 and whole numbers from 10, a trailing .0 dropped (9.96 kB reads 10 kB); a value that rounds to 1000 of a unit is shown in the next
rules.details: refusal, note and issue details are creator sentences and are not pinned; codes and fields are
rules.secrets: a string holding <<secret:NAME>> stands for secretFixtures[NAME] joined; a runner expands every marker (in keys and values) before answering

cases.name: plan: a pair only NTFS merges is refused too (the as-spelt fold)
cases.note: NTFS upper-cases each unit and does not normalise: U+0345 then U+0307 is ι then U+0307 there. Normalising first moves U+0345 after U+0307, so the macOS fold alone misses it; a path is inside the folder under either fold.

cases.name: plan: the macOS fold decomposes before it folds case
cases.note: ᾳ (U+1FB3) then a caron is, under NFD, α, the caron, then U+0345, which folds to ι: APFS finds it as α, caron, ι. Folding the composed ᾳ first gives α ι and then the caron, and misses it.

cases.name: plan: a folder spelt in another Unicode normal form still holds the world file
cases.note: APFS ignores normalisation: É as E and U+0301 (NFD) is é (NFC) there. Both sides are NFC before folding.
